title: Deterministic subquadratic dynamic s–t reachability
formal: Do there exist constants \(\varepsilon>0,C>0,p\in\mathbb N\) and one uniform deterministic data structure that, for every \(n\ge2\), maintains a directed graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) under single-edge insertions and deletions, and answers reachability queries for designated vertices \(s,t\in V\), with both update time and query time at most \(C n^{2-\varepsilon}\) in the worst case? Initialization from the explicit initial graph must take at most \(C n^p\) time, and the data structure must use at most \(C n^p\) words throughout every operation sequence. The designated pair is given at initialization and remains fixed. Every answer must be exactly correct after all preceding updates, for every finite, adaptively chosen sequence of updates and queries.

source_formulation.text: Can fully dynamic st-reachability be solved deterministically in subquadratic time?
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 2

why: Reachability is a basic directed-graph primitive, and frequent edge changes make recomputing its answer expensive. A deterministic worst-case guarantee applies to every update sequence and every individual operation. The historical question identifies whether a polynomial improvement over quadratic maintenance is possible without randomness.
status_note: Resolved positively by van den Brand and Karczmarz in the same FOCS 2023 paper from which the question was extracted. The deterministic branch of Theorem 1.1, proved as Theorem 6.3, has subquadratic worst-case update and query time. The individual review checked the source theorem and relevant proof/model passages; it does not claim an independently formalized Lean proof.

importance.reason: Deterministic fully dynamic directed reachability is a fundamental test of whether fast graph maintenance can avoid probabilistic correctness and adversary restrictions. A polynomial saving below the quadratic barrier is a substantive advance for general directed graphs, with significance reinforced by the stronger exact-distance result that resolves this historical question.

sentences: This historical question asks for deterministic maintenance of directed reachability under edge insertions and deletions.
Both each update and each fixed-pair query must take worst-case time with a fixed polynomial saving below quadratic.
The computational model charges word operations, preprocessing and all retained state.
The source paper itself gives a stronger deterministic exact-distance result with exponent 1.969.
The completed record is archived as resolved because the imported question was separated from its answer in the same introduction.

definitions: The graph is unweighted and has no parallel edges; loops may be omitted. The vertex set remains fixed. An insertion adds one absent directed edge \((u,v)\), and a deletion removes one present edge. A legal update sequence satisfies these conditions when each update is issued. Reachability is true exactly when there is a directed path from \(s\) to \(t\) in the current graph; a path of length zero is allowed, so \(s=t\) always returns true. The initial graph is supplied as its \(n\)-by-\(n\) binary adjacency matrix, together with \(n,s,t\); an update gives its type and two vertex identifiers. A query requests one Boolean answer. Time is measured on a sequential word RAM with \(w=d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits per word, for a fixed sufficiently large integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm. One instruction reads or writes a word, branches, compares words, applies a bitwise Boolean operation or logical shift, or performs addition, subtraction, multiplication modulo \(2^w\), integer quotient or remainder with a nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Addresses fit in a word, and arithmetic on longer integers is charged for its constituent word operations. The program is finite and independent of \(n\), with no advice, free precomputed tables, random bits or arithmetic oracle. All initialization and table construction are charged. The worst-case bounds apply to each completed operation separately, including any maintenance it performs; averaging expensive operations across a sequence does not satisfy them. Constants are independent of the graph, its designated pair, sequence length and sequence contents. Polynomial space may be reused indefinitely and includes all maintained state. This specifies the ordinary deterministic time version of the source question, not an unbounded-precision unit-cost arithmetic model.
answer_criterion: The historical benchmark asks for a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed existence assertion or its negation. A positive answer must provide a uniform deterministic data structure and establish exact reachability, polynomial initialization and space, and a common fixed polynomial saving below quadratic worst-case time for updates and queries. A negative answer would have to exclude every positive \(\varepsilon\) under these conventions. An amortized bound, a randomized guarantee, or a result allowing only insertions or only deletions is insufficient. The published positive resolution determines this card’s archival status; that editorial classification is not itself a Lean-checked implementation or proof.

context_blocks.text: The imported sentence is Open Problem 2 in the introduction of the 2023 paper. The very next paragraph states that the paper answers it. Treating the extracted question as still open omitted the result immediately following it. The complete reviewed card is therefore preserved in the inactive archive.

Theorem 1.1, proved as Theorem 6.3, gives a deterministic data structure for unweighted directed graphs with \(O(n^{1.969})\) worst-case time for each single-edge update and for an exact-distance query from an arbitrary source to all vertices. This stronger query functionality establishes the requested fixed-pair reachability assertion. The paper accounts for the nonconstant cost of arithmetic on its longer coefficients.

The deterministic result must be distinguished from the faster Monte Carlo alternative in the same theorem. It also differs from the paper’s all-pairs results and from updates that change every edge incident to a vertex. The historical reachability question here uses individual edge changes.
